why: Sightread's 60-second demo: ask what a change breaks, answer twice (with the parsed import graph and without it), and count the gap. Every number here was measured on Express with Kimi K3.1 Pro over Cerebras; nothing is invented, and the same model both times.
prompt: If I change lib/application.js, what breaks?

answer.lead: 100 files sit downstream of that one file.
bullets: the same model with no graph named 13 of the 100

claim.unit: of 100 files, named with the graph
claim.footnote: *Measured on Express with Kimi K3.1 Pro on Cerebras: 21 of 100 named with the graph in 1.23 s; the same model without it named 13 in 9.75 s.

thread.text: Parsed the repository · 142 files, 160 internal imports
The list is computed from the import statements, not guessed. Handing it to the model is the whole trick: it answers from evidence instead of rebuilding a hundred-file blast radius from memory.
